reasoning: 1. TARGET ENGAGEMENT: No biomarker data available to assess whether atezolizumab engaged PD-L1 or whether enzalutamide engaged AR. The trial provides no PD/PK data or target engagement biomarkers. 2. PATHWAY MODULATION: No pathway biomarkers reported to assess whether checkpoint blockade activated T-cell immunity or whether androgen receptor antagonism was achieved. 3. CLINICAL TRANSLATION: The primary endpoint (overall survival) was not met. HR 1.184 (95% CI: 0.971-1.445), p=0.094 indicates the combination was numerically worse than enzalutamide alone, though not statistically significant. 4. POPULATION EFFECTS: No subgroup analyses reported. 5. CONFOUNDERS: The trial appears adequately powered (n=759) and had appropriate duration (182.6 weeks). Safety profile showed higher AE rates in combination arm (96.8% vs 92.3%) but no dose-limiting toxicity that would prevent adequate dosing. This appears to be a clean efficacy failure where the combination hypothesis was tested but did not improve outcomes.

failure_modes.evidence: Primary endpoint missed with adequate power and duration. No biomarker data to confirm target engagement, but the failure pattern suggests the combination biology may have been active but did not translate to survival benefit in this population.
